sections.h2: Which Robertson County offices value and bill my property?
sections.html:
Two elected offices in Springfield divide the job. The Assessor of Property puts a value on land and buildings, while the County Trustee mails the bills and takes in the money. A third office, the Register of Deeds, files the deeds that link them.

  • Assessor of Property: Chris Traughber, 521 S. Brown St., Springfield, 615-384-4311, weekday hours 8 to 4:30.
  • County Trustee: Kendra Shelton, Room 161 of the Robertson County Office Building, 515 S. Brown St., 615-384-4238, Monday through Friday until 4:30 p.m.
  • Register of Deeds: John West, same weekday schedule.

The trustee reported that in 2025 the office collected about $60 million in property tax payments on more than 40,000 parcels. That volume is why a seller should ask for payoff figures in writing instead of relying on a phone estimate.

sections.h2: What does a seller in Robertson County need to know about the local housing market?
sections.html:
Robertson County sits on the Kentucky line and belongs to the Nashville metropolitan area. Census estimates show 80,175 residents as of mid 2025, a gain of 10.1 percent over the 2020 base of 72,809.

The typical owned home is valued at $335,000 (2020 to 2024 figures), household income runs $83,047, and owners occupy 77.6 percent of homes. Rent is modest: $1,199 a month at the median, below neighboring Rutherford County. With 476.34 square miles of land, density is only 152.8 people per square mile.

Springfield is the county seat. Other incorporated places include Adams, Cedar Hill, Cross Plains, Greenbrier, Orlinda, Coopertown, Ridgetop and White House, while Millersville and Portland sit mainly in Sumner County. Interstate 65 follows the eastern border for about 20 miles, and Interstate 24 runs along the southwestern border for about 10 miles.

sections.h2: What is the Robertson County tax calendar, and what does late payment cost?
sections.html:
The window opens the first Monday of October and closes with the final day of February. After that, state law adds 1.5 percent interest on March 1 and again at the start of every later month.

Robertson County real property tax calendar
StepWhat happensSource
January 1Owner on this date carries tax liability for the tax yearCounty Trustee
First Monday of OctoberTaxes become payable; notices go out in early October when the commission has set the rateCounty Trustee
Last day of FebruaryFinal day to pay without interest (Friday, February 27 for the 2025 bill)County Trustee
March 11.5% interest begins, T.C.A. 67-5-2010County Trustee
March 15Last day to pay a year-delinquent bill at the trustee officeCounty Trustee
March 16 to 31Delinquent real property goes to the tax attorney, then a Chancery Court suit, T.C.A. 67-5-2404County Trustee

The 2025 deadline of February 27, 2026 has passed. The 2026 bill follows the same pattern, so ask the trustee for the final in-office day if the 28th lands on a Saturday or Sunday.

sections.h2: Where can I send a Robertson County tax payment?
sections.html:
Counter, mail, web, phone and bank draft all work. While a bill remains in the trustee office, partial payments and prepayments are accepted.

  • In person: Room 161 of the county office building during office hours, or the drop box by the sliding front door.
  • Drive thru: a kiosk lane at the office building.
  • Local banks: The Farmers Bank (all branches) and United Community Bank in Springfield, current year only and October through February, with the paper notice in hand.
  • Online or phone: tnproptax.com or 1-877-556-4079. The vendor charges 2.50 percent on cards or $1.25 on e-checks, plus $0.30 for phone payments, and the county keeps none of it.
  • Mail: the postmark date counts for interest.
  • Auto draft: monthly on the 10th, with the enrollment form received before the first of the prior month.

Most mortgage servicers remit in December, and the trustee suggests verifying the posting at tnproptax.com well ahead of March 1.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax if a Robertson County house sells mid-year?
sections.html:
Liability sits with whoever owned the property on January 1, according to the trustee, though a sales contract can shift the cost. The trustee keeps no record of such contracts, and the duty to confirm payment stays with you.

The Assessor adds a timing detail: a copy of each recorded deed arrives the next day, and roughly 90 days pass before the parcel carries the buyer's name. The bill goes to whatever name was on file January 1 until the following year, and the closing papers should say who pays. Tax notices are not mailed to the mortgage company.

Before closing, ask the trustee for a current balance on every parcel you own. The trustee warns that deeds are indexed under different spellings of a name, so a search by name alone can miss a parcel.

sections.h2: What is the route for disputing a Robertson County assessment?
sections.html:
Disputes move from the Assessor's office to the local equalization board and then to the state board. Tennessee's Appeals Handbook notes that county boards ordinarily open on June 1 and stay in session as long as the caseload needs.

Someone unhappy with the county board's answer has until August 1 of that tax year, or 45 days after the notice date if that is later, to file at the state level (T.C.A. 67-5-1412(e)). Processing cost is capped at $10 per filing. Values are fixed as of January 1, so events after that date are generally irrelevant to the value, and the handbook treats recent comparable sales as the strongest evidence of a house's value.

Search by owner name, address or parcel number on the state-run Tennessee Property Data site that the Assessor links to, then check the record against the actual house.

sections.h2: What relief and special programs does the Robertson County Trustee run?
sections.html:
The trustee's page lists three programs for eligible owners: a Tax Relief Program, a Tax Freeze Program and a Wheel Tax Rebate. In 2025 the office reported roughly 950 people in the freeze program, about 1,200 in the relief program and about 135 wheel tax rebates.

Farmland owners should also know about greenbelt. The Assessor mails greenbelt applications within 90 days of a processed deed. If land leaves agricultural, forest or open space use, rollback taxes apply: the difference between use value and market value for the preceding three years for farm and forest land, or five years for open space. They are not a penalty and become delinquent March 15 of the following year (T.C.A. 67-5-1008(d)). Anyone selling acreage should ask the Assessor whether a change of use is coming.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Robertson County house that still has tax due?
sections.html:
Yes, the balance is simply handled as part of the sale. Every buyer, lender and title company will want the exact figure, so request it from the trustee in writing.

Timing changes the process. While a real property bill is under one year delinquent, it stays with the trustee, who accepts partial payments. Once it is turned over, payment goes through Robertson County Chancery Court at 615-384-5650 and extra costs attach. Delinquent personal property tax for 2015 through 2024 can be paid through American Financial Credit Services at 888-317-2327 extension 3.

A cash purchase can go forward with a tax balance outstanding, though you should weigh the payoff against the price offered. Have the settlement statement list the trustee payoff on its own line.

faqs.q: What is the Robertson County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: Late February ends the interest free period. For the 2025 bill that final day was Friday, February 27, 2026, and 1.5 percent interest started March 1.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Robertson County?
faqs.a: Room 161 of the county office building, 515 S. Brown St. in Springfield, takes payments, as do the drop box, the drive thru, two named local banks, tnproptax.com and the mail.

faqs.q: How long does a deed take to show up with the Robertson County Assessor?
faqs.a: About 90 days. The Assessor gets a copy the day after recording, then moves the parcel into the new owner's name. The tax bill goes to the January 1 owner until the next year.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Robertson County assessment after the county board meets?
faqs.a: Yes. The State Board of Equalization takes appeals filed by August 1 or within 45 days of the county board's notice, whichever comes later. Begin with the Assessor at 615-384-4311.

faqs.q: Does Robertson County have a property tax relief program for seniors?
faqs.a: The Trustee runs a Tax Relief Program and a Tax Freeze Program. Call 615-384-4238 for eligibility rules and application timing, because the trustee sets the current requirements.
